Real reported account 638b2999-2866-47a6-bd37-22e80453bc4d verified via tests/test_iter21_real_account_check.py: DB state {phone: +918291026526, email: None, billing_email: lloydmasih1976@gmail.com, identity_type: phone} — /auth/me returns identity='+918291026526', identity_type='phone', email=null. The startup migration has already moved this user's stray email to billing_email as expected. Navigated to the AGENTS tab and asserted testID='account-identity' text: (a) phone case = '+919835851483' matches the phone that signed in, (b) email case = 'iter21-310d752c@example.com' matches the email — the exact acceptance criteria in the review request. Screenshots at /tmp/iter21_phone_ok.png and /tmp/iter21_email_ok.png. No red screen, no console errors of substance (only 'Animated: useNativeDriver not supported' RN-Web boilerplate and a benign 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated' from a third-party lib). AUTH_DEBUG_RETURN_OTP restored to false, backend restarted, confirmed. Full backend regression: 519 passed / 44 xdist-flaky failed / 9 skipped in the -n2 --dist loadscope run — but every failing file re-run serially (-n 0) passes cleanly (114/114 across test_identity_display, test_portfolio_api, test_refactor_regression, test_security_fixes_iter16/21, test_wallet_razorpay_admin) — matches the review-request warning that Yahoo/LLM/Razorpay e2e are load-flaky under xdist. Total sequential pass across the suite matches the 562/9 baseline plus this session's 8 new identity tests + 1 real-account probe.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/auth_routes.identity_type_for is conservative in the RIGHT direction: an account with a phone AND a legacy stray email is treated as 'phone' unless google_sub/apple_sub/identity_type explicitly says email — that is what actually fixes lloydmasih1976@gmail.com bleeding onto +918291026526's card, because the pre-fix /pay/order was the only writer that could have set users.email on a phone signup and it could never have verified it.

server.py::migrate_unverified_billing_email is idempotent by construction (it only touches rows where users.email is set AND identity_type != 'email' AND google_sub/apple_sub are unset — after the first pass, users.email is None so the second pass is a no-op) — matches the test that runs it twice inside one asyncio.run(). The one-loop constraint is genuine and correctly documented in the test.

AccountCard.tsx line 19 keeps `user.identity || user.phone || user.email || 'Signed in'` as a defensive fallback — reasonable because /auth/me pre-populates identity, but a very old cached SessionUser from before this deploy would still fall back to phone/email locally. Not a bug; note only.
api.ts SessionUser exposes identity_type as `'phone' | 'email'` — matches the two values the backend actually emits.

rca_of_issue: Original bug: signing in with +91829… showed lloydmasih1976@gmail.com on the ACCOUNT card. Cause: legacy POST /api/pay/order wrote the email the user typed for their Razorpay receipt directly onto users.email, and AccountCard rendered `user.email || user.phone` — so any unverified email overrode the actual sign-in identity. Fix (verified): (1) backend now records identity_type on new accounts and exposes both identity_type + identity on /auth/me and /auth/otp/verify; (2) resolver defaults to 'phone' unless google_sub/apple_sub/identity_type='email' says otherwise, so a legacy row with a stray email still resolves to its phone; (3) startup migration moves users.email → billing_email for phone accounts with no verified-email evidence (log confirmed 'moved 3 unverified emails' on preview DB, including the reported user); (4) AccountCard now renders user.identity. Reproduction of the ORIGINAL bug is no longer possible on this codebase — the reported user id now returns identity='+918291026526' from /auth/me.
